title: Hierarchical fanout + probabilistic sketch aggregator for low-latency console metrics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current console metrics pipeline struggles with very large tenants that emit high-cardinality usage patterns and hot keys, producing spikes in downstream aggregator latency and increased egress cost. We need a streaming pattern that preserves low 95th/99th latency for API customer dashboards while bounding memory/cost for worst-case tenants.

This ticket proposes a hierarchical fanout + probabilistic sketch aggregator design:
- Ingress gateway performs light-weight routing to a small set of local aggregators based on tenant hash + shard version.
- Local aggregator performs early, time-bucketed pre-aggregation using Count-Min Sketch for high-cardinality counters and K-MinSketch (or Top-K sketch) for heavy-hitter detection, plus HyperLogLog for approximate unique counts.
- Probabilistic sketches are propagated downstream in a bounded-size message; a downstream combiner performs mergeable sketch reductions and emits final approximations for dashboards and billing pipelines.
- A hierarchical fanout allows routing to a short-circuit path for SLA-critical tenants (pin to dedicated aggregator), and to multi-tenant aggregated paths for low-volume tenants.
- Implement adaptive sampling: when a tenant's per-second event rate exceeds a threshold, switch ingress to reservoir-sampling + sketching to bound throughput while preserving heavy-hitter accuracy.

Goals:
- Maintain 95th percentile end-to-end pipeline latency <= 300ms under 95% load profile.
- Bound per-aggregator memory usage so a single tenant spike cannot OOM the node.
- Keep final dashboard errors within defined tolerances (e.g., <2% for top-10 counters, <5% for mid-cardinality approximations).

Non-goals: exact counts for every counter, replacing detailed per-request audit logs (those remain a separate store).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress can switch tenants to reservoir-sample+sketch path when rate thresholds exceeded
End-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 300ms on our staging traffic profile
Memory per aggregator bounded to < 3GB at 99th percentile under synthetic spike tests
Sketch merge correctness validated with unit tests and integration tests (relative error metrics recorded)
Rollout plan with canary routing and a fallback to exact-aggregator within 5 minutes

2026-02-15 - Owen Patel: Proof-of-concept local aggregator implemented (rust). Tested Count-Min + HLL libraries; memory footprint promising. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ingest/pull/819

2026-02-20 - Lena Fischer (SRE): Ran fault-injection tests. Observed that heavy-hitter detection loses accuracy when reservoir sampling ratio < 0.1 for 99th-percentile traffic. Recommend a hybrid path that pins top-K items for hot tenants.

2026-03-03 - QA: Integration test harness added. Running 24h soak against production replay data (sanitized). Observed sustained 20% reduction in downstream bytes for high-cardinality tenants.

2026-03-05 - Owen Patel: Rebased PoC branch and opened new PR for ingress routing logic. TODO: add metrics for sketch error distribution and tie into Console SLO dashboard. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ingest/pull/872
notes: Trade-offs: sketches provide bounded memory but are approximate. We plan a two-phase rollout: (1) non-critical tenants switched to sketching to gather error distributions; (2) enable sampling for heavy tenants and expose pinning for Dedicated customers. Must monitor for edge cases where approximations cause billing divergence; contingency is to fall back to exact-mode for affected counters.
test_plan: Unit tests for sketch merge + serialize/deserialize
Integration test using production replay with configurable tenant-rate overrides
Chaos test: kill aggregator nodes during merges to validate idempotent merges and checkpoint recovery
Latency SLO tests using k6 to simulate multi-tenant traffic patterns
